note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 9478 / 出力 8481 トークン

data.assessment: In this busy period the current rules (block_k 2, SLA 120 s / 120 s) deliver 219.4 of 222.8 orders on time, with 3.4 late, no unfinished orders and p95 wait 93.2 s, so at most about 3.4 on-time deliveries remain to gain. Blocking (1217 s) and road violations (34.8: release 17.8, blocking_guard 17.0) are still the main friction, concentrated on B (3.0 late, 521 s blocked) and C (25.1 penalty points, lowest utility at 46.9). Road violations are higher than the 28.0 measured when block_k 2 was adopted. That is the persisting cost the human said would trigger reconsideration, but busier demand may explain part of the rise.

proposals.title: block_k 2 -> 1 (evict a road-parked robot as soon as one robot waits behind it)
proposals.rationale: Blocked time is still 1217 s and B, the company with the most blocking, accounts for most of the 3.4 late deliveries. Lowering block_k again should cut blocking and the late deliveries it causes, much as 3 -> 2 halved blocked time and added +7.2 on-time. The ceiling is small (about 3.4 orders), so the gain may not clear the 1.0 improvement threshold. A, which does not park on the road, likely votes yes. C, and probably B, likely vote no because evictions are Major sanctions, so this would again need an override.
proposals.cadl:
# =====================================================================
# robot_town.cadl ─── ロボットの街：3 社の配送ロボットが道路を共有する
#
# 道路網はラズパイマウスのシミュレータと同じ 11 ノード・17 エッジ。
# 3 社（A / B / C）が 2 台ずつロボットを走らせ、ノードは 1 台ずつしか
# 使えない。仕事のないロボットは車庫に戻るか、道路上（中央の交差点 8）
# に止まって次の注文を待つ。止まったロボットは他社の通行をふさぐ。
#
# `# @amend:<名前>` が付いた行は、改正してよいパラメータ。どの層（規則・
# 契約）に属し、どこまで動かしてよいかは constitution.yaml が決める。
# 委員会（COUNCIL）が自分で改正できるのは規則の層だけで、契約の層を
# 変えるには人間の判断が要る。
# =====================================================================

sos:
  name: "RobotTown"
  type: Collaborative             # 独立した 3 社が共通の規則を決める
  version: "1.0.0"

  context:
    environment:
      num_robots:   6
      num_companies: 3
      time_step_ms: 1000

  actors:
    - id: TOWN_STEWARD
      role: "road_steward"
      autonomy: low
      capabilities: [assign_order, record_violation, evict]
      interface:
        input:  [order_request, position_report, node_released, rule_update]
        output: [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, violation_report]

    - id: "ROBOT[1..N]"
      role: "delivery_robot"
      autonomy: high
      capabilities: [move, park, pickup, dropoff]
      interface:
        input:  [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, amendment_proposal]
        output: [position_report, node_released, ballot]

    - id: COUNCIL
      role: "rule_amendment_body"
      autonomy: medium
      capabilities: [propose_amendment, tally_ballots]
      interface:
        input:  [violation_report, ballot]
        output: [amendment_proposal, rule_update]

  contracts:
    # ── 顧客への約束：注文 1 件ごとのインスタンス（契約の層。人間が決める） ──
    - id: DELIVERY_SLA
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]"]
      guarantee:
        - "pickup_time <= 120s"         # @amend:pickup_deadline
        - "dropoff_time <= 120s"        # @amend:dropoff_deadline
      lifecycle:
        states: [Assigned, PickedUp, Delivered, Late]
        initial: Assigned
        terminal: [Delivered, Late]
        transitions:
          - id: pickup
            from: Assigned
            to:   PickedUp
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == PickedUp"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:pickup_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }
          - id: dropoff
            from: PickedUp
            to:   Delivered
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == Delivered"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:dropoff_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }

    # ── 道路の使い方：道路上に止まるたびに 1 インスタンス ──
    - id: ROAD_USE
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]", COUNCIL]
      guarantee:
        - "hold_time <= hold_limit"
      authority:
        decision_holder: COUNCIL
        beta: 0.5
        mode: "collective"
      information:
        alpha: 1.0                    # 規則と違反記録は全社に公開
      incentives:
        type: sanction
        lambda: 0.5                   # @amend:sanction_lambda
        rules:
          - "penalty(ROBOT[i], lambda) when overstay"
      lifecycle:
        states: [Holding, Overstay, Released, Evicted]
        initial: Holding
        terminal: [Released, Evicted]
        transitions:
          - id: release
            from: [Holding, Overstay]
            to:   Released
            on:   "ROBOT[i] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
            deadline: 60s             # @amend:hold_limit
            on_violation: { transition: Overstay, severity: Minor }
      monitors:
        - id: blocking_guard
          observe: "ROBOT[i].blocking"
          sampling: periodic(1000ms)
          rule: "ROBOT.blocking >= 1 AND state IN [Holding, Overstay]"  # @amend:block_k
          on_match: { transition: Evicted, severity: Major }

  # ── 運用モード：分散（各社が道路上で待つ）⇄ 集中（管理者が待避所を割り当てる） ──
  # 条件は 5 分ごとに、直前 5 分の観測で判定する。
  #   orders_in_window : 3 社の注文の合計件数
  #   blocked_pct      : ロボットが止まっているロボットにふさがれていた時間の割合（%）
  # 集中管理は交差点をふさがれない反面、エッジを 1 台ずつ割り当てるので、
  # 注文が非常に多いと許可待ちが積み重なる。そのときだけ分散に戻す。
  transitions:
    - from: DISTRIBUTED
      to: CENTRALIZED
      condition: "orders_in_window < 22"      # @amend:to_central
      protocol: SWITCH
      safety_invariant: "robots_on_road == 0"
    - from: CENTRALIZED
      to: DISTRIBUTED
      condition: "orders_in_window >= 26"     # @amend:to_distributed
      protocol: SWITCH

  protocols:
    - id: SWITCH
      trigger: "regime_condition_holds"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> ROBOT[*] : regime_notice"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
        - "TOWN_STEWARD : activate_regime"
    - id: AMEND
      trigger: "period_end"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> COUNCIL : violation_report"
        - "COUNCIL -> ROBOT[*] : amendment_proposal"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> COUNCIL : ballot"
        - "COUNCIL : tally_ballots"
        - "COUNCIL -> TOWN_STEWARD : rule_update"

  metrics:
    - id: on_time_deliveries
      formula: "count(Delivered)"
      target: ">= 0.9 * count(orders)"
    - id: blocked_time
      formula: "sum(blocked_robot_seconds)"
      target: "<= 600s"
proposals.why_human: The vote is likely to fail (C and probably B against), so adoption would mean a second override. In D2 the human limited overrides to consistent multi-period customer gains, and the remaining gain here is at most about 3.4 orders. Road violations, whose safety meaning is unknown, already rose to 34.8 and would likely rise further; the human said this would trigger reconsideration.
assumptions: Most remaining late deliveries are caused by robots parked at intersection 8 blocking others.
Evicting at one waiting robot does not create extra travel that delays the evicted company's own deliveries.
A does not park on the road (0 road waits, 0 penalty), so it bears no eviction cost.
unknowns: Whether the gain reaches the 1.0 minimum improvement given the 3.4-order ceiling.
How much road violations and C's sanctions would increase.
The safety meaning of road violations, which the human flagged as unknown.

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: Small gain, likely +0.5 to +2; may fail the 1.0 threshold.

predictions.subject: vote:A
predictions.note: A is blocked but never parks, so it gains.

predictions.subject: vote:B
predictions.note: B parks often (62 road waits) and would incur more Major sanctions.

predictions.subject: vote:C
predictions.note: C already carries 25.1 penalty points and would lose more utility.

proposals.title: hold_limit 60s -> 50s (shorter allowed stop on the road)
proposals.rationale: Release overstays (deadline:release 17.8) are the largest violation cause, and blocked time is still 1217 s, mostly hitting B. A shorter hold limit could free intersection 8 sooner under busy demand. In period 2 this step gained only +0.4 on 2/5 seeds under different rules and demand, so this re-measures it under block_k 2 and busy demand, not on the same evidence. A likely votes yes and C likely votes no; any on-time gain is probably small.
